data.narrative:
Etched, a Series E chip design company founded by Gavin Uberti, Chris Zhu, and Robert Wachen, is evaluated against a frontier-semiconductor peer set comprising 8 private companies and 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD). The target currently carries a $5.0B post-money valuation on $800M total raised.

Two valuation methods apply directly. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to the $5.0B Series E post-money and applying a typical 1.4x step-up multiplier to next financing stage, implies $7.0B. Peer-median analysis across 4 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies (SambaNova Systems at $11.0B, Ayar Labs at $3.8B, Tenstorrent at $2.7B, Nearfield Instruments at $1.6B) yields a median valuation of $3.2B, with a range spanning $1.6B to $11.0B. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied; the public Semiconductors median P/S is 20.4x across three tickers, but Etched's revenue is not disclosed, precluding this method.

Triangulating the two applicable methods produces a range of $2.7B (low) to $8.0B (high), with a median of $5.1B. The current $5.0B valuation aligns closely with the triangulated median, suggesting fair value at present post-money. Material uncertainty stems from the wide peer dispersion ($1.6B to $11.0B) and the absence of revenue data, which limits precision in public-market anchoring and precludes revenue-multiple cross-checks.
